findings.finding: The fix's core assumption — that `claude -p <pointer>` combined with piped stdin content actually causes the CLI to treat stdin as (or append to) the effective prompt — could not be empirically verified in this environment (Bash calls referencing the `claude` binary are sandboxed against recursive invocation) and remains unverified beyond indirect prior-behavior evidence.
findings.evidence: claudeAdapter.ts:154-167, 268-279; confirmed via git show 5a78078^ that the removed comment described the CLI waiting ~3s for stdin data it wasn't given, implying it does check stdin when a positional prompt is present — suggestive but not conclusive proof of the combining semantics.
findings.recommendedAction: Watch the next real --full run that hits the Integrator role on a large multi-implementer task (e.g. bl_368a454b itself) and confirm from its actual behavior/log that it received and acted on the full task content, not just the pointer sentence. If it turns out stdin is ignored when a positional arg is also given, the fix would need to drop the positional prompt argument entirely rather than keep it as a pointer.

notes: Reviewed the actual commit (5a78078) in this worktree independently, not the prior summary. Root cause is well-supported: contextBuilder.ts confirms systemPromptAddition (still passed via --append-system-prompt in argv) is bounded to fixed role/company docs, while userPrompt (via renderUserPrompt) is where prerequisiteArtifacts — the unbounded, per-task-size implementer reports the Integrator uniquely aggregates — actually land. Repo history has a real precedent of a >40k-line prerequisite artifact (frontend-implementation.md/changed-files.json in an earlier task dir), corroborating that this field really can blow past argv/environ limits. The fix correctly targets exactly that field: buildClaudeArgs() now pushes a small fixed STDIN_PROMPT_POINTER instead of options.userPrompt, and runProcess() pipes the real userPrompt over stdin (stdio changed from ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] to ['pipe','pipe','pipe'], with a no-op error listener on child.stdin to avoid an unhandled-stream-error crash on early child exit). The stdin-wait ~3s comment being replaced was itself evidence the CLI already reads stdin alongside a positional prompt in the pre-fix state, which is consistent with (though not conclusive proof of) the standard-usage-pattern claim. Diagnostics for the second failure mode (silent exit 1) genuinely improved: the close handler's error message now includes exit signal, stdout bytes received, and total argv bytes. Verified independently: `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run test` 157/157 passing including the new regression tests (args not containing the huge prompt, and a 5MB-prompt test proving total argv bytes stays under 100KB). `git show --stat` confirms only the 4 claimed files changed, matching the report exactly — no scope creep. `hangWithChild.mjs` fixture and its one caller in processLifecycle.test.ts were updated consistently (pidfile now read from stdin, not argv), and I confirmed the sibling fixtures (hangGraceful.mjs/hangIgnoreSigterm.mjs) don't depend on argv/stdin prompt content at all, so nothing there was silently broken by the transport change. This is orchestrator-internal infra work, not a rentals/ product feature, so QA's usual browser/mobile/T&S review scope correctly doesn't apply here — the orchestrator's own automated suite is the right gate, and it passes. The implementer's own self-check note honestly flags the one real residual risk (unable to empirically invoke the real `claude` binary from this sandbox to confirm stdin+positional-prompt combining semantics) and recommends watching the next real large-diff Integrator run to confirm empirically — I agree that's the right next step and don't consider it a blocker for this diff, since the design is conservative (keeps a real positional arg rather than betting on an unverified 'no-prompt, stdin-only' mode) and is bounded by directly-observable prior CLI behavior (the removed 3s-wait comment).
